_doc: Research-gap matrix and objective-to-module map. Sources: the PhD proposal (Final5, November 2026), its reference list, the systematic scoping review (140 studies) and the 5 November 2026 audit. Every study cited here is in the proposal's reference list. Figures marked 'project finding' come from this project's own analyses, not from published literature.

sources.proposal: 01_Proposal/Final5_An Integrated Earth-Observation, IoT and Edge-AI System ... .docx
sources.review: 02_Systematic_Review: scoping review of 140 studies; counts are studies reaching each step of the evidence chain
sources.not_done: No new literature search was run for this matrix. The literature library (529 records) has not been searched in Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore or ACM directly, so the gap statements for the embedded-systems questions rest on targeted journal searches.

legend.project: This project's own finding, not yet peer reviewed
legend.proposed: Proposed contribution or hypothesis, not yet tested

gaps.topic: Forecasting new surface water, not only detecting existing water
gaps.accomplished: Satellite radar maps open and vegetated water that exists now (Hardy et al. 2019; Vanderhoof et al. 2023; Tran et al. 2022).
gaps.limitations: These studies classify the present. A map made on the day of a flight is out of date for water that forms afterwards. In the scoping review, 3 of 140 studies made a prospective forecast.
gaps.gap: No study forecasts, site by site, which dry locations will hold new water days ahead and tests that forecast against a simple recent-water rule on forecasts archived before the outcome.
gaps.rinda: Issues and archives 7- and 14-day forecasts for 600 monitoring locations, replays any past issue using only data available then, and shows each forecast beside the recent-water baseline.
gaps.evaluation: Difference in 7-day PR-AUC between the model and the recent-water rule B1 on publicly archived forecasts, lower 95% confidence limit above zero.
gaps.status: Preliminary, and narrowed by the 13 November 2026 correction. With Sentinel-1C and 1D corrected, PR-AUC is 0.599 (7 d) and 0.569 (14 d) against 0.534 and 0.484 for B1 (published before correction: 0.786 and 0.663). 95% of events are at the lake shore; inland there is no demonstrated skill. H1 needs forecasts archived before outcomes.

gaps.topic: Linking forecast water to Anopheles habitat suitability
gaps.accomplished: Habitat characteristics explain larval presence at surveyed water bodies: a model predicted An. funestus-positive habitats with 83% accuracy in Tanzania (Kahamba et al. 2024); model ensembles improved habitat maps in western Kenya (Zhou et al. 2024); a hydrological model predicted ponding in Ethiopia (Jiang et al. 2021).
gaps.limitations: These describe habitats that already exist and were surveyed. Only a minority of water bodies hold larvae: 11.2 to 16.5% in rural Tanzania (Msugupakulya et al. 2024). In the review, 31 studies predicted larval habitat and none predicted productive habitat.
gaps.gap: Forecast water has not been filtered to likely Anopheles habitats using routine programme records.
gaps.rinda: Keeps water (target A) and confirmed breeding (target D) as separate models. Accepts RBC survey files as versioned datasets and records dipping results in the field workflow. No habitat model exists yet.
gaps.evaluation: PR-AUC for Anopheles larval presence against a habitat-type-only rule, on survey visits held out by site block and season, then on random dipping samples.
gaps.status: Awaiting data. RBC historical records were requested on 14 October 2026.

gaps.topic: Combining Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, weather and terrain
gaps.accomplished: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 have been compared for water mapping over long time series (Vanderhoof et al. 2023).
gaps.limitations: Fusion is usually assumed to help. It is rarely tested by removing one source at a time on a forecasting task.
gaps.gap: Whether optical, weather and terrain data add forecasting skill beyond radar history at site level.
gaps.rinda: Model Assurance reports ablation by source. The data inventory lists Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Landsat, terrain and surface-water holdings with dates, resolution and quality.
gaps.evaluation: Change in PR-AUC when a source is removed, with block-bootstrap intervals.
gaps.status: Project finding that challenges the proposal's starting assumption: rainfall and temperature, including archived numerical forecasts, added no measurable skill once radar history and orbit geometry were in the model.

gaps.accomplished: Larval development sets the useful lead time: pupation after about 8 days for An. arabiensis and 10 to 13 days for An. funestus in Tanzanian field habitats (Msugupakulya et al. 2024).
gaps.limitations: Forecast horizons in the literature are rarely tied to the treatment window.
gaps.gap: How much skill is lost between 7 and 14 days, and whether a 14-day lead is usable.
gaps.rinda: Evaluates and displays the two horizons separately and warns that 14-day forecasts are weaker.
gaps.evaluation: Separate PR-AUC, precision and recall per horizon on identical periods.
gaps.status: Project finding: 14-day alert precision missed its 0.75 target (0.72), and on February to September 2026 the retrained model was no better than the frozen one (0.674 against 0.677).

gaps.topic: Field larval verification joined to remote-sensing predictions
gaps.accomplished: Drone imagery finds water bodies well, but in one study only 31.9% of confirmed water bodies contained larvae (Francisco et al. 2026). Drone-visible habitat features were associated with larval presence in Malawi (Stanton et al. 2021).
gaps.limitations: In the review, 2 of 140 studies verified targets in the field. Programme surveys are not random and record positives more than negatives.
gaps.gap: Predictions are seldom checked by dipping at the predicted place, with absences recorded.
gaps.rinda: Inspection tasks from forecasts, an offline field form that separates 'not sampled' from 'none found', supervisor review, and a dossier that keeps predicted, observed and confirmed evidence apart.
gaps.evaluation: Share of confirmed water bodies with Anopheles larvae by habitat type, from a random sample chosen independently of the model.
gaps.status: Built, awaiting field data. RBC entomology team requested, not confirmed.

gaps.topic: IoT sensing as a ground reference
gaps.accomplished: Low-cost water-level sensors and LoRa links are mature (Ding et al. 2025; Dao et al. 2025; Kabi et al. 2023).
gaps.limitations: They are used for hydrology, not to check when a satellite first sees water or to calibrate water thresholds.
gaps.gap: Satellite water labels lack a ground reference for presence and onset.
gaps.rinda: Authenticated telemetry endpoint, node registry, stored readings with units and range flags, delivery ratio, and a sensor layer on the map. No node is commissioned.
gaps.evaluation: Paired F1 difference between thresholds calibrated on sensor data and on Sentinel-2, each node held out in turn; detection delay described.
gaps.status: Interface built, awaiting hardware in the field.

gaps.accomplished: Networks have been benchmarked on the Jetson Orin Nano, where the steps before and after inference take a large share of total time (Szegedi et al. 2026). Lightweight water segmentation exists (Cao et al. 2025), and a quantised detector has run on a drone FPGA (Rosi et al. 2026).
gaps.limitations: Models are usually chosen by FLOPs or inference-only latency, and by averages, not by the slowest runs of the whole pipeline.
gaps.gap: Whether choosing by measured 99th-percentile full-pipeline latency gives a different and better model than proxy measures.
gaps.rinda: Flight-log analytics (latency distribution, deadline-miss ratio, stage tails). Records size, inference time and memory for every trained forecast model on the server. The onboard water model does not exist yet.
gaps.evaluation: Deadline-constrained F1 on untouched data for configurations chosen by p99 latency, FLOPs and inference-only latency.
gaps.status: Awaiting the onboard model and Jetson measurements. Server timings in RINDA are not edge measurements.

gaps.topic: From habitat intelligence to targeted drone larviciding
gaps.accomplished: Drones already apply Bti in Rwandan rice fields, with a 95.3% fall in Anopheles larval density in a non-randomised trial (Munyakanage et al. 2024). Drone mapping with image analysis found over three times as many sites and cut larvicide use by more than 60% in Ghana (Bokpin et al. 2026). Lag compensation reduced mean spray lag from 3.87 m to 0.32 m (Wang et al. 2023).
gaps.limitations: Mapping and treatment are separate passes, a day or more apart (Bokpin et al. 2026; Hardy et al. 2023). Compensation uses average delays; an RTK system still missed target starts and ends by about 0.9 m (Lyu et al. 2025).
gaps.gap: No system links a forecast to a mission, and no validated method predicts whether a camera-triggered spray is on time and on target (the core of the thesis).
gaps.rinda: Inspection flights from forecasts; treatment missions only from supervisor-authorised habitats; approval, exports without spray commands, flight results. The timing-and-placement controller is studied outside RINDA; RINDA ingests its logs.
gaps.objective: Objective 2 (mission link) and Objective 3 · RQ6 · H6a to H6c (core)
gaps.evaluation: Calibration of predicted treatment probability; share of eligible targets treated with controller C3 against C2; non-inferior off-target fraction.
gaps.status: Mission workflow built. Controller hypotheses untested.

gaps.accomplished: Larviciding reduces vectors when enough productive habitats are found and treated; in the review, 9 studies measured an intervention outcome.
gaps.limitations: In the review, 1 of 140 studies delivered a targeted intervention from a prediction. In Ghana, malaria case trends did not differ between study arms (Bokpin et al. 2026).
gaps.gap: Whether forecast-guided treatment reaches new habitats sooner than a two-pass workflow.
gaps.rinda: Indicators from records only: inspection and treatment turnaround, follow-up completion, habitats positive more than once, coverage of positive habitats. Malaria incidence is not measured.
gaps.evaluation: Time from water onset to confirmed treatment, analysed as interval-censored; share treated before late instars; cost per positive habitat treated.
gaps.status: Awaiting an approved study with RBC. Probably an estimation study, not a trial of health impact.

gaps.topic: Data availability, resolution, generalisation and uncertainty
gaps.accomplished: Published models report accuracy on the area and period they were built in.
gaps.limitations: Random splits of correlated satellite samples overstate skill; few studies test a frozen model in a second area or publish calibrated uncertainty.
gaps.gap: Transfer without retraining, honest uncertainty, and labels that measure the intended thing.
gaps.rinda: Temporal splits with an embargo, held-out 500 m blocks, calibration plots, conformal sets, a model registry where approval is explicit, and the audit warning on every forecast.
gaps.objective: Objective 2 · RQ3 · H3, and all objectives
gaps.evaluation: Frozen model against B1 on identical site-days in a second area; coverage of prediction sets; label agreement with ground readings.
gaps.status: Project finding (audit): 83 to 87% of events lie within 100 m of the lake; Sentinel-1C verifies 73 to 80% of evaluation events and is not harmonised; 297 of 598 evaluated sites are outside the sector. A second area is not yet selected.

challenges.title: The label does not measure marshland water
challenges.detail: Corrected on 13 November 2026: once Sentinel-1C and 1D were put on the Sentinel-1A reference, almost all inland 'new water' disappeared and 98% of events lie at the lake shore. The forecast is a lake-shore forecast; at 50 m with these radar thresholds new inland water is barely detected.
challenges.recommendation: Describe the served forecast as lake-shore only. For the marshland, design a label for small or vegetated water and check it against in-situ sensors (RQ4) and field visits.

challenges.title: Weather did not help
challenges.detail: The proposal expected rainfall to drive formation. In this valley the model's skill came from radar history, orbit geometry and terrain. This fits managed or lake-driven water more than rain-fed pools.
challenges.recommendation: State this finding plainly in Paper 1 and test it again on inland sites after relabelling.

challenges.title: A simple baseline is hard to beat
challenges.detail: The first model lost to a 30-day water-frequency rule. Later versions beat it, but partly on data that was not blind.
challenges.recommendation: Register the forecast archive before outcomes are known, as H1 requires, and keep the baseline on every screen.

challenges.title: Programme records are not a random sample
challenges.detail: RBC surveys go where staff expect larvae, with varying dipping effort. A habitat model trained on them describes where RBC looks.
challenges.recommendation: Model detection effort, and validate on the random dipping samples of Studies 3 and 5 before any water body is skipped.

challenges.title: The forecast model is not the edge model
challenges.detail: The forecast runs on a ground server. Latency, memory and power on the Jetson concern the onboard water-segmentation model and the spray controller, which are not built yet.
challenges.recommendation: Keep server timings and edge measurements apart, as RINDA now does.

challenges.title: Sites were sampled by water frequency
challenges.detail: Monitoring locations were chosen using water frequency in a box around the sector, so about half lie outside it and few are on the valley floor.
challenges.recommendation: Define the study population for the marshland explicitly, with official boundaries from NISR or RBC.

objectives.text: Forecast new surface water 7 to 14 days ahead against a recent-water baseline, and predict which forecast water becomes Anopheles larval habitat and how long remains before pupation.
objectives.delivered: Forecast display, replay, baselines, dataset registry, reproducible training, model registry, field verification workflow.
objectives.open: Label reconstruction after the audit; prospective archive for H1; RBC entomological records for the habitat model (H5).

objectives.text: Carry the forecast to the field: test transfer to a second area, check satellite water labels against in-situ sensors, and link forecasting, sensing, drone or ground allocation and mission planning.
objectives.delivered: Telemetry endpoint and node registry, sensor layer, connectors that wait for approved access, mission planning with approval, suitability assessment that assigns drone or ground treatment.
objectives.open: Sensor nodes in the field; a second area; an agreed rule for assigning habitats to drone or ground teams.

objectives.paper: Paper 3: edge AI and deadline-aware spraying
objectives.text: Choose the onboard water model by measured end-to-end latency, and develop and validate a probabilistic timing-and-placement controller for single-pass spraying.
objectives.delivered: Flight-log ingestion and analytics (latency distribution, deadline-miss ratio, verification precision and recall), mission records, server-side efficiency measurements.
objectives.open: The onboard model, the controller, Jetson and flight measurements. These are experiments outside the console; RINDA records and analyses their logs.
